name: Formal linkers: whereas, while, since, as, given that
subtitle: Use whereas and while to set two different facts side by side, and as, since and given that to give a reason. These linkers sound more formal than but and because. Tom likes tea, whereas Mia prefers coffee. Since the shop is closed, we'll go tomorrow.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-b2 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: Tom likes tea, whereas Mia prefers coffee. · Since the shop is closed, we'll go tomorrow. · Given that it is late, we should go.

qa.html: whereas and while compare two different facts. Each side is true: My brother lives in the city, whereas I live in a village. Mia works in an office, while her sister works from home. The clause can come first or second. In the middle, put a comma before the linker. At the start, put a comma after the first clause: Whereas Tom likes tea, Mia prefers coffee. Whereas is more formal. While can also mean "at the same time", so the sentence must make the meaning clear.

as and since give a reason that the reader already knows or can see. They usually start the sentence: As it was raining, we stayed at home. Since the shop is closed, we'll go tomorrow. Do not add so in the second part. Because is the normal word when the reason is new information.

given that means "taking this fact into account". It is formal. Given that the train is late, we will miss the start. She did well, given that she had no training. Seeing that works in the same way and is a little less formal. Before a noun alone, use given without that: Given the weather, we stayed in.

These linkers belong more to writing and formal speech: reports, essays, emails to a manager. In everyday talk people say but (contrast) and because or so (reason). Use the formal linkers when you want your text to sound careful and organised.

Typical mistakes: ✗ Tom likes tea. Whereas Mia prefers coffee. → ✓ Tom likes tea, whereas Mia prefers coffee. (whereas starts a clause, not a new sentence) · ✗ Given the weather was bad, we left. → ✓ Given that the weather was bad, we left. (before a clause use given that) · ✗ As it was late, so I went home. → ✓ As it was late, I went home. (no so after as or since)

concept.noteHtml: Whilst is a formal British form of while. While, as and since can also talk about time: Since 2019 I have lived here. You find time clauses in time clauses and for, since, ago. In this topic the sentence always shows a contrast or a reason. For although, however and despite see contrast. Whereas compares two different things; although says that something is surprising: Although it was cold, we went out. For pairs like both … and see paired conjunctions.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose the linker you hear. You can listen twice.

items.text: My brother loves football, whereas I prefer tennis.
As it was raining, we stayed at home.
Given that the flat is so small, the rent seems high.
Mia works in an office, while her sister works from home.
Since you are tired, let's stop here.
Seeing that it is late, we should go.

rounds.label: 1 · two facts → whereas
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences about two different things. Join them with whereas, with a comma before it.

example.prompt: My father lives in the city. My mother lives in the country.
example.answer: My father lives in the city, whereas my mother lives in the country.

items.prompt: Tom likes tea. Mia likes coffee.
items.answer: Tom likes tea, whereas Mia likes coffee.

items.prompt: The north is cold. The south is warm.
items.answer: The north is cold, whereas the south is warm.

items.prompt: I work in an office. My husband works from home.
items.answer: I work in an office, whereas my husband works from home.

items.prompt: Trains are fast. Buses are cheap.
items.answer: Trains are fast, whereas buses are cheap.

items.prompt: Priya takes the bus. Liam rides a bike.
items.answer: Priya takes the bus, whereas Liam rides a bike.

items.prompt: Winter is dark here. Summer is bright.
items.answer: Winter is dark here, whereas summer is bright.

rounds.label: 2 · reason → since
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences. The second one is the reason. Start with Since and the reason, then say the result.

example.prompt: We stayed at home. It was raining.
example.answer: Since it was raining, we stayed at home.

items.prompt: We took a taxi. It was late.
items.answer: Since it was late, we took a taxi.

items.prompt: I can't come. I have to work.
items.answer: Since I have to work, I can't come.

items.prompt: She stayed in. She felt ill.
items.answer: Since she felt ill, she stayed in.

items.prompt: Let's eat out. The fridge is empty.
items.answer: Since the fridge is empty, let's eat out.

items.prompt: He didn't answer. He was driving.
items.answer: Since he was driving, he didn't answer.

items.prompt: We can't go in. The museum is closed.
items.answer: Since the museum is closed, we can't go in.

exercises.title: whereas, since or given that? Complete the sentences.
exercises.hint: Is the sentence comparing two different things (contrast) or giving a reason?
exercises.hintHtml: whereasTwo different facts side by side: A, whereas B.as / sinceA reason that is already known: Since A, B.given that / seeing thatA fact to take into account (formal).

items.prompt: My brother loves the city, ___ I prefer the countryside.
items.why: Two people with different tastes: contrast, so whereas.

items.prompt: ___ the shop is closed, we'll buy the bread tomorrow.
items.why: The closed shop is the reason: since or as.

items.prompt: Trains are quick, ___ buses are cheaper.
items.why: Trains and buses are compared: contrast, so whereas.

items.prompt: ___ you have already paid, you don't need to pay again.
items.why: Having paid is the reason, formal: given that.

items.prompt: Mia works in an office, ___ her sister works from home.
items.why: Two sisters, two different ways of working: contrast, so whereas.

items.prompt: ___ it was raining, we stayed at home.
items.why: The rain is the reason for staying in: as.

items.prompt: Most shops open at nine, ___ the market opens at seven.
items.why: Shops and market have different times: contrast, so whereas.

items.prompt: ___ you are already here, let's have lunch together.
items.why: Being here is the reason: seeing that.

exercises.hint: Keep the meaning. The formal linker starts a clause, so the clause needs a subject and a verb. Choose the correct sentence.
